summary: Václav Machek was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Josef Zubatý and also studied under Antoine Meillet, Theodor Bloch, and Sylvain Lévi. He was later Docent of IE Linguistics at Masaryk University.
W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. D. Rouse was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Regent's Park College and Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Fellow and Sanskrit Lecturer at Christ's College, Cambridge, and Headmaster at The Perse School.

W. H. R. Rivers was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields who studied medicine at the University of London. He served as Lecturer in Psychology at Cambridge, Fellow at St John's College, and President of the Royal Anthropological Institute.

W. Haskell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Dartmouth College and Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at East Maine Conference Seminary and served as a librarian at Yale from 1875 to 1905.

W. Norman Brown was an Indologist and historian. He completed his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and studied under Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Johns Hopkins and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1926–1966).

W. Randolph Kloetzli worked in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies, completing his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago in 1964. He studied under mentors including Milton Kleintop and J. A. B. van Buitenen, and lectured at American University.

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was a Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.
W. W. Tarn was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at Eton College and Trinity College, Cambridge, where he later became a Fellow.

Wadigala Samitharathana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford, and became Founding President and Managing Trustee of the Oxford Buddhist Society in 2023.

Wai-lun Tam works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning a Ph.D. from McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara. His appointments include professor and Chairperson in Cultural and Religious Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walenty Skorochód Majewski was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Collegium Nobilium, where he became a teacher in 1785, and was placed in charge of the Central Archives of Historical Records in 1808.

Walpola Rahula was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon, University of Calcutta, and Sorbonne under Paul Demiéville. He served as Professor at Northwestern University and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura.

Walter A. Fairservis, Jr. was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Chicago, Columbia, and Harvard. He held curatorial posts at the American Museum of Natural History, directed the Burke Museum, and was a professor at Vassar College.

Walter Anthony Cook was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Woodstock College, De Nobili College, St. Mary's College, Kurseong, and Georgetown University, where he later served as Professor of Linguistics from approximately 1966 to 1993.

Walter Bruno Henning was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Göttingen under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding posts at SOAS (1936–1961) and as Professor of Iranian Studies at UC Berkeley (1961–1967).

Walter Clawiter was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt between approximately 1952 and 1958, and later held a post there.

Walter Couvreur was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven under Albert Joseph Carnoy and at Göttingen under Emil Sieg, later serving as Professor of IE Linguistics at Ghent University.
Walter Denecke was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Hamburg by 1923. He studied under Hermann Jacobi and Walther Schubring.

Walter Elliot was a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St. George, he served as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Madras.
